title: SLO contract drafting & benchmark roadmap - Hawthorn (POC kickoff)
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark config template (link) and raw script by 2025-11-03
Hawthorn to provide representative sample traffic and 7 days of traces by 2025-11-06
Schedule infra prep call to validate VPC peering and firewall rules week of 2025-11-10
Redwood to provide pilot estimate and recommended Dedicated config by 2025-11-07
action_items: Sofia Martinez - draft benchmark YAML and measurement plan - due 2025-11-03
Liam O'Connor - export 7 days of production traces + payload size histogram - due 2025-11-06
Jordan Park - send security pack + SOC2 snapshot and KMS integration notes - due 2025-10-30
Ethan Wu - run quick synthetic run on sample model variant and send initial TTFT/TPOT estimate - due 2025-11-05
summary: Kickoff to define POC acceptance criteria for latency/throughput SLOs. Main focus: agree on TTFT vs TPOT targets, sampling strategy (p95/p99), traffic composition, and an executable benchmarking roadmap. Identified action items: Redwood to share benchmark template and security docs; Hawthorn to provide traces and payload distributions. Timeline: aim to run pilot measurements in mid-November and agree acceptance matrix by end of November.
topics: TTFT vs TPOT definitions and tradeoffs
traffic sampling and synthetic vs replay benchmarks
KV cache / warm vs cold path considerations
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for pilot
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-28 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Jordan Park, Sofia Martinez, Ethan Wu (Redwood); Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Marta Silva, Carlos Pinto (Hawthorn)

[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone thanks for carving time, we wanted to use this to nail down the acceptance criteria for the POC and the benchmark roadmap. Sofia and Ethan from our team will go into measurement detail.
[00:25] Priya Nair: thanks Jordan, quick context — Hawthorn's main user flows are the query assistant in our analytics UI and a nightly batch enrichment job. The UI is interactive, target median roughly sub-200ms for first token ideally. Nightly is throughput-heavy.
[01:10] Sofia Martinez: okay great, that maps to the classic TTFT versus TPOT split. for clarity, when I say TTFT I'm meaning time-to-first-token from request arrival to server sending first byte. TPOT is total per-token time for full response. we usually define SLOs for both depending on flow.
[01:45] Liam O'Connor: can you also define in practice what we measure? is TTFT measured at the edge or inside the instance? we have client and ELB timing differences.
[02:10] Ethan Wu: good question. our recommendation is to measure TTFT at the synthetic client to include network overhead for hosted trials, but for dedicated/VPC you may want both tcp-level from upstream LB and service-level internal timing. we supply a measurement harness that emits both.
[02:45] Marta Silva: and p95/p99 — we need to know which to contract on. our SRE favors p99 for the UI path, product team leans p95 because of cost.
[03:20] Jordan Park: right. typical pattern — p95 for customer-visible UI for non-blocking flows, p99 for blocking interactive SLOs. but we can craft a weighted acceptance: e.g., UI primary route p95 < 200ms and p99 < 350ms, else fallback to smaller model with graceful degrade.
[03:55] Carlos Pinto: are those numbers realistic given the model sizes? we run a trimmed T5-like open model ~7B, mostly quantized to int8 right now.
[04:25] Sofia Martinez: with 7B on GPU and warm KV cache, hitting TTFT under 200ms is plausible for short prompts (<=128 tokens). for longer prompts or cold cache, TTFT can spike. That's why we recommend defining warm vs cold sample buckets.
[05:00] Priya Nair: what's your recommended sample ratio between warm and cold? our product experiences cold more because we spin up ephemeral containers.
[05:25] Ethan Wu: for POC benchmarking I'd suggest a 70/30 warm/cold mix representative of your real traffic, but also include a worst-case 100% cold sweep to show tail behavior. we'll help you stitch traffic from traces to build that mix.
[05:55] Liam O'Connor: about TPOT — for the nightly batch we care about throughput (tokens per second) and cost. can you help translate TPOT into instance sizing?
[06:20] Sofia Martinez: yes, we'll run throughput profiles across burst and sustained runs. TPOT effectively maps to tokens/sec and GPU utilization. we'll produce an estimate table: expected TPOT at 90% util -> GPUs required for X qps.
[06:45] Priya Nair: how do you handle KV cache misses in the measurement harness? the assistant uses cached prefixes a lot.
[07:10] Ethan Wu: our harness can replay KV cache hits by preloading sessions into the runtime. though real prefix caching depends on routing and sticky sessions. we'll document assumptions. sometimes transcription shows KV as K V which is weird in our logs, but yes we handle it.
[07:40] Jordan Park: one more upfront contract thought — should acceptance be strictly numeric thresholds or include qualitative regression checks (e.g., hallucination rate on specific prompt set)?
[08:05] Carlos Pinto: product asks for both; numeric SLOs for latency and throughput, and quality gates for a small eval set. we can accept a small drop in model perplexity but not a spike in hallucinations on our compliance prompts.
[08:35] Sofia Martinez: we recommend a two-tier acceptance: 1) performance SLO matrix (TTFT p95/p99, TPOT sustained) and 2) quality evaluation with baseline prompts. both must pass.
[09:00] Priya Nair: ok let's try to specify concrete numbers now for the UI route. propose p95 TTFT <= 220ms, p99 <= 430ms?
[09:25] Liam O'Connor: those p99 numbers feel high, can we aim lower if we use Dedicated?
[09:40] Jordan Park: yes Dedicated typically gets better tail because of warmed instances and reserved pools. for Hosted we usually add a 15-25% buffer on tail due to multitenancy. we can propose a Dedicated pilot target p95 <= 180ms p99 <= 300ms.
[10:05] Marta Silva: we need to capture methodology — measure load, concurrency, distribution of prompt lengths. We'll share 7 days of traces with tokens and payload sizes.
[10:30] Ethan Wu: perfect. include timestamped traces and sequence length distributions. we'll convert to synthetic queries for replay and also run a replay on a staging cluster to compare.
[10:55] Carlos Pinto: what's the cadence for benchmarks? single run or multiple sweeps?
[11:15] Sofia Martinez: multiple. plan: cold sweep (single-run cold start), warm steady-state sweep (30m sustained at representative qps), burst sweep (short 2-5m high qps), and tail sensitivity tests (inject large payloads). each yields TTFT and TPOT distributions.
[11:45] Priya Nair: measurement artifacts — what do you deliver? CSVs? dashboards?
[12:00] Jordan Park: we deliver a structured report: raw CSVs of per-request timings, aggregated percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), tokens/sec graphs, and a short deck with recommendations. we'll also include a mapping to instance sizing and monthly cost estimate.
[12:30] Liam O'Connor: can your harness capture backend queuing time vs GPU compute time? we need to separate queuing induced by batching.
[12:55] Ethan Wu: yes we instrument kernel times, batching wait time, and net. some labels are best-effort because kernels are model-specific. we'll annotate confidence levels.
[13:20] Sofia Martinez: also want to surface sequencing effects — e.g., when many small requests vs few large ones interact. we'll run mix profiles.
[13:40] Priya Nair: about SLO enforcement — if pilot misses p99 by 20% do we fail POC?
[13:55] Jordan Park: that's why we recommend a graded acceptance matrix. example: green if p95 and p99 within target, yellow if p95 within but p99 slightly above (<20% over) with mitigations, red if both fail. decisions on go/no-go should be agreed in advance.
[14:25] Carlos Pinto: can we use a weighted SLO? our route mix is 90% short and 10% long. weighted latency might favor short requests.
[14:45] Sofia Martinez: yes we can compute weighted percentiles — we'll label them and show both route-level and weighted global SLOs.
[15:10] Liam O'Connor: security and data residency — we plan to use VPC private deployment for sensitive flows. will that change measurement?
[15:30] Ethan Wu: network topology will affect raw TTFT. for VPC we recommend internal measurements and a small network latency overlay. We'll document that in the report. Also note KMS/HSM for keys — Jordan will send the integration notes.
[15:55] Jordan Park: I'll send the security pack and SOC2 snapshot today.
[16:10] Priya Nair: thanks. about model variants — could fallback to a smaller quantized model for tail mitigation be an acceptance tactic?
[16:30] Sofia Martinez: yes that fits our graceful degradation story. part of the benchmark we'll test a fallback chain: primary model, compressed variant, and default template response. measure switch latency too.
[17:00] Carlos Pinto: can Redwood run the benchmarks on our cloud account or do you prefer to run from Redwood-hosted infra?
[17:20] Ethan Wu: either. Hosted run is faster to start but includes multitenant noise. running in your VPC (private) gives cleaner results for Dedicated sizing. For initial POC we suggest Redwood-hosted replays plus a final run in your VPC.
[17:45] Liam O'Connor: licensing and cost — we need a pilot price for a 2-week dedicated reserved capacity test.
[18:00] Jordan Park: we'll provide a pilot estimate after we see the trace volume and traffic profile. action: we'll give a ballpark then refine.
[18:20] Priya Nair: talk me through the benchmark template you send.
[18:35] Sofia Martinez: the template contains: traffic mix, prompt length buckets, sampling ratios (warm/cold), run durations, concurrency schedule, and the metrics to capture (TTFT at p50/p90/p95/p99, TPOT aggregated tokens/sec, GPU util, and error rates). We also include reproducible scripts and a short README.
[19:10] Carlos Pinto: can we include a small quality test — 30 prompts we care about — and measure latency and model output drift?
[19:30] Sofia Martinez: yes we will run a quality check pre/post model variants and flag regressions.
[19:50] Liam O'Connor: what about synthetic vs traffic replay — does replay preserve arrival distribution and session affinity?
[20:10] Ethan Wu: replay preserves exact sequences if you use the trace-replay tool but you need to be careful with identifiers and rate shaping. We'll provide a safe replay config and a synthetic generator for scaled tests.
[20:40] Priya Nair: let's lock on specific numeric targets for the POC acceptance matrix. I'm hearing two sets: Hosted and Dedicated. propose: Hosted UI route: TTFT p95 <= 250ms p99 <= 450ms; Dedicated UI route: TTFT p95 <= 180ms p99 <= 300ms. For nightly batch: TPOT sustain >= 250k tokens/min (example).
[21:25] Jordan Park: sounds reasonable as a starting point. We'll include those as initial proposals in the benchmark template and we'll allow one tuning window after the first runs.
[21:50] Marta Silva: sampling strategy: we want the p99 to be computed on at least N requests — what's the minimum sample size?
[22:10] Sofia Martinez: p99 requires enough samples; rule of thumb is to have at least 1000 samples for stable p99 estimates. we'll recommend run lengths to meet that.
[22:40] Carlos Pinto: and regression tolerance? how much deviation is allowed?
[22:55] Jordan Park: we'll propose thresholds: green within target, yellow if p99 up to 20% over, red if beyond that. quality regressions are strict — any new hallucination on compliance prompts is red.
[23:20] Priya Nair: ok good. timeline — when do we expect the first benchmark runs?
[23:35] Ethan Wu: if you share traces by 2025-11-06, we can prepare configs and run Redwood-hosted synthetics by 2025-11-12 and an in-VPC run by 2025-11-18. final acceptance review end of November 2025-11-28.
[24:00] Liam O'Connor: that timeline works.
[24:15] Jordan Park: quick note on reporting: we'll give raw artifacts and a short executive summary showing acceptance matrix and recommended actions.
[24:30] Priya Nair: any risks we should log?
[24:45] Sofia Martinez: risks: sample mismatch (traces don't reflect true distribution), cold-start variability, and model quantization impacting quality. We'll log mitigations in the plan.
[25:10] Carlos Pinto: anything about auto-scaling affecting results?
[25:25] Ethan Wu: yes autoscale policies can change observed tail; for the POC we recommend fixed reserved capacity to measure deterministic behavior then test autoscaling separately.
[25:50] Priya Nair: ok. can you show an example deliverable?
[26:05] Jordan Park: we'll attach a sample report link in the followup — sample: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/sample-report (placeholder).
[26:25] Liam O'Connor: how do you account for tokenization differences across model variants?
[26:45] Sofia Martinez: we normalize by tokens emitted; we also record input tokenization to ensure consistent label. some differences may be due to differing vocab splits; we'll include per-request token counts.
[27:05] Carlos Pinto: please also call out any assumptions in the report e.g., concurrency distribution, exact model weights used.
[27:25] Ethan Wu: yes assumptions section will be upfront.
[27:45] Priya Nair: do you have any checklist for us to prepare traces for safe sharing? we are careful with PII.
[27:55] Jordan Park: yes we'll send a minimal PII checklist and sanitized export guidance. action: Jordan to send security pack and trace export checklist.
[28:15] Marta Silva: fine. also would like to know how you'll handle jitter in cloud networking for hosted runs.
[28:35] Sofia Martinez: we'll annotate network jitter by running a control ping baseline and subtracting that from TTFT; again we'll show internal vs external timings.
[29:00] Priya Nair: OK I'm happy with the plan. let's confirm the action items and dates.
[29:15] Jordan Park: recapping actions: Jordan send security docs (today); Sofia send benchmark template (by 2025-11-03); Hawthorn provide traces (by 2025-11-06); Ethan run initial synthetic run and share rough pilot estimate (by 2025-11-05). Intent: first Redwood-hosted runs by 2025-11-12, in-VPC by 2025-11-18, acceptance review 2025-11-28.
[30:00] Carlos Pinto: sound good. one last question — will you include cost tradeoff analysis?
[30:15] Jordan Park: yes we'll include per-route cost per 1M tokens at the tested configs and a recommended Dedicated plan.
[30:35] Priya Nair: great thanks everyone.
[30:45] Liam O'Connor: thanks.
[30:50] Marta Silva: bye.
[31:00] Jordan Park: thanks team. We'll send the follow up and links.

End of recording. (exported transcript shows speaker attribution may be imperfect in a few places; occasional mis-heard tokens and abbreviations)
